In-class Exercise 7: Floating Catchment Area Accessibility

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source
Author

JUNCHEN LI

Published

October 17, 2026

Overview

This classroom exercise compares four floating catchment area approaches to eldercare accessibility in Singapore. It uses the supplied In-class_Ex07.zip data and adapts its R workflow, whose original document lists Xiaohan as author. The numerical model code is retained; the introductory text and website presentation have been expanded for this learning portfolio.

Demand is set to 100 for every hexagon and capacity to 100 for every facility. These are teaching assumptions, not measured elderly populations or service capacities. The resulting maps illustrate model behaviour rather than current service adequacy.

Data and preparation

Extract the supplied archive into this exercise folder, keeping data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv and the complete shapefile components in data/geospatial. The spatial layers are Master Plan 2014 subzones, a prepared hexagonal grid, and eldercare locations. Use these matched inputs together rather than substituting newer layers independently. GIS metadata files ending in .qmd are not Quarto pages and are excluded from the website source folder.

1 Loading R packages

Installing catchment R package from github

Run the following installation commands manually only when the packages are missing. They are displayed but not executed during rendering. This GitHub link installs software; the exercise data come from the supplied course archive.

Show code 
install.packages("remotes")
Show code 
remotes::install_github('uva-bi-sdad/catchment')

Next, load sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility and catchment R packages into RStudio environment using the code chunk below

Show code 
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment)

2 Importing and preparing the data

The three spatial layers are transformed to Singapore SVY21 (EPSG:3414). Network costs in the supplied OD table are converted from metres to kilometres. Matrix rows must correspond to the hexagon order and columns to the facility order before the accessibility scores are attached to the map.

Next, use the code chunk below to import OD_Matrix.

Show code 
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
Rows: 375000 Columns: 6
── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Delimiter: ","
dbl (6): origin_id, destination_id, entry_cost, network_cost, exit_cost, tot...

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.

Use the code chunk below to create a new field called demand and populate value 100 in it.

Show code 
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)

Use the code chunk the select origin_id, destination_id and total_cost of ODMatrix data frame. Then, rename them to from_id, to_id and dist respectively.

Show code 
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)

In the code chunk below as.matrix() is used to convert the data frame into matrix object.

Show code 
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)

In this code chunk below, catchment_ratio() of catchment package is used to compute 2SFCA.

Show code 
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
Show code 
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")

3 Mapping 2SFCA

The two-step floating catchment area model first relates facility capacity to demand within a catchment, then aggregates the available supply-to-demand ratios for each demand location. Here, max_cost = 5 defines a five-kilometre network-distance catchment.

Show code 
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)
Show code 
hex_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)

4 Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

E2SFCA introduces stepped distance-decay weights: nearby opportunities receive greater weight than more distant opportunities. The supplied thresholds span one to five kilometres. These weights are illustrative assumptions rather than empirically calibrated travel preferences.

Show code 
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
Show code 
hex_E2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_e2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_E2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "E2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("E2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)

5 Gaussian Kernel 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

This variant applies the package's Gaussian weighting option to introduce smooth distance decay. Its defaults are retained from the supplied exercise. This is a distance-weighted accessibility model, not a point-pattern kernel density map.

Show code 
df_kd2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = "gaussian") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("KD2SFCA" = ".")
Show code 
hex_KD2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_kd2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_KD2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "KD2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,

  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +

  tm_scalebar() +

6 3-Step Floating Catchment Area

The final variant uses the stepped weights with normalize_weight = TRUE. This changes how demand is allocated across competing providers. Compare its spatial distribution with the earlier models while keeping the demand, capacity and network inputs fixed.

Show code 
df_3sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights,
  normalize_weight = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("3SFCA" = ".")
Show code 
hex_3SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_3sfca)
tm_shape(hex_3SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "3SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("3SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)

Interpretation and limitations

The four maps use model-specific rounded intervals (style = "pretty", with five intervals requested). This presentation-only adjustment replaces the supplied ten-quantile classification, which produced repeated breakpoints and misleading interval labels where many scores were zero. The model calculations are unchanged. Because each map has its own range, the same colour need not represent the same score across models. Compare the legend values and underlying scores before drawing conclusions about differences in magnitude. The original reversed blue palette is retained: darker colours indicate lower accessibility.

The uniform demand and capacity assumptions, historical teaching layers, distance-decay choices and supplied network matrix limit real-world interpretation. The imported subzone layer provides geographical context but is not used in the accessibility calculations below. These maps do not test statistical significance or establish actual unmet need.

# Overview

This classroom exercise compares four floating catchment area approaches to eldercare accessibility in Singapore. It uses the supplied `In-class_Ex07.zip` data and adapts its R workflow, whose original document lists Xiaohan as author. The numerical model code is retained; the introductory text and website presentation have been expanded for this learning portfolio.

Demand is set to 100 for every hexagon and capacity to 100 for every facility. These are teaching assumptions, not measured elderly populations or service capacities. The resulting maps illustrate model behaviour rather than current service adequacy.

## Data and preparation

Extract the supplied archive into this exercise folder, keeping `data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv` and the complete shapefile components in `data/geospatial`. The spatial layers are Master Plan 2014 subzones, a prepared hexagonal grid, and eldercare locations. Use these matched inputs together rather than substituting newer layers independently. GIS metadata files ending in `.qmd` are not Quarto pages and are excluded from the website source folder.

# 1 Loading R packages

Installing catchment R package from github

Run the following installation commands manually only when the packages are missing. They are displayed but not executed during rendering. This GitHub link installs software; the exercise data come from the supplied course archive.

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("remotes")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false

```


Next, load sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility and catchment R packages into RStudio environment using the code chunk below

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment)
```

# 2 Importing and preparing the data

The three spatial layers are transformed to Singapore SVY21 (EPSG:3414). Network costs in the supplied OD table are converted from metres to kilometres. Matrix rows must correspond to the hexagon order and columns to the facility order before the accessibility scores are attached to the map.

```{r}
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                    layer = "hexagons") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                     layer = "ELDERCARE") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

Next, use the code chunk below to import OD_Matrix.

```{r}
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```

Use the code chunk below to create a new field called demand and populate value 100 in it.

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

Use the code chunk the select origin_id, destination_id and total_cost of ODMatrix data frame. Then, rename them to from_id, to_id and dist respectively.

```{r}
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)
```

In the code chunk below as.matrix() is used to convert the data frame into matrix object.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```

In this code chunk below, catchment_ratio() of catchment package is used to compute 2SFCA.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```


```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

# 3 Mapping 2SFCA

The two-step floating catchment area model first relates facility capacity to demand within a catchment, then aggregates the available supply-to-demand ratios for each demand location. Here, `max_cost = 5` defines a five-kilometre network-distance catchment.
```{r}
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)
```

```{r}
hex_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "2SFCA",

                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,

  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +

  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

# Interpretation and limitations

The four maps use model-specific rounded intervals (`style = "pretty"`, with five intervals requested). This presentation-only adjustment replaces the supplied ten-quantile classification, which produced repeated breakpoints and misleading interval labels where many scores were zero. The model calculations are unchanged. Because each map has its own range, the same colour need not represent the same score across models. Compare the legend values and underlying scores before drawing conclusions about differences in magnitude. The original reversed blue palette is retained: darker colours indicate lower accessibility.

The uniform demand and capacity assumptions, historical teaching layers, distance-decay choices and supplied network matrix limit real-world interpretation. The imported subzone layer provides geographical context but is not used in the accessibility calculations below. These maps do not test statistical significance or establish actual unmet need.
